_note: Concept preview range. Every scent is a SAMPLE: names, notes, stories and colours were written for the preview and are not the client's. No prices: they come from the client.

families.title: Fresh
families.blurb: Citrus, green leaves, cold water. The scents you reach for in the morning.

families.title: Floral
families.blurb: Rose, jasmine, iris. From a single pressed petal to a whole night garden.

families.title: Woody
families.blurb: Cedar, vetiver, smoke. Dry, quiet and long lasting.

families.title: Warm
families.blurb: Honey, amber, resins. Close to the skin and made for the evening.

scents.name: Common at dawn
scents.story: The first walk across the common before anyone else is up. Grass still wet, the air green and a little bitter, a cold brightness that burns off by nine. Worn close, it stays sharp and clean for the length of a morning and then settles to a soft mossy skin scent.

scents.name: Lido at seven
scents.story: An early swim in unheated water: the shock of it, then the calm. Lemon and salt up front, a clean floral middle, and a dry driftwood base that lasts into the evening. The one fresh scent here that holds its own at a dinner table.

scents.name: Rose on paper
scents.line: A pressed rose, iris and cotton
scents.story: Not a rose in a garden; a rose kept flat between the pages of a book. Papery, powdery and faint, with the iris giving it a cool, old-fashioned softness. The quietest scent in the range and the easiest to wear every day.

scents.name: Jasmine, late
scents.story: Jasmine opens at dusk and is strongest after dark, which is when this is meant to be worn. A spiced tea opening gives way to a full white-flower heart and a creamy sandalwood base. Big enough for a party, but still smooth.

scents.name: Cedar wardrobe
scents.line: Pencil cedar, iris and clean linen
scents.story: The smell of the inside of a cedar wardrobe when the door opens: dry wood, a little pencil shaving, clean linen that has been folded for a while. Soft and tidy rather than smoky. Sits well on anyone and under anything else.

scents.name: Smoke and fig
scents.line: Green fig, birch smoke and vetiver
scents.story: A fig tree next to a bonfire. The milky green of the fruit against dry, resinous smoke, with a deep vetiver and oud base that lasts until the next morning. The darkest scent in the range and the one people ask about.

scents.name: Honey, burnt
scents.line: Dark honey, amber and vanilla pod
scents.story: Honey taken to the point where it almost catches: sweet, slightly bitter, a little smoky. Beeswax and tobacco leaf keep it from being a dessert; the amber base keeps it close to the skin for hours. For cold evenings and good coats.
